title: Is removing citizens forever ‘national interest’? Arunachal’s Siang Valley simmers after crackdown

ai.summary: Residents in Arunachal Pradesh's Siang Valley protested against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, demanding the release of detained activists and halting pre-feasibility studies after clashes with security forces and arrests.

facts.claim: Residents called for a halt to all pre-feasibility studies towards the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project
facts.quote: residents called for a halt to all pre-feasibility studies towards the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project

facts.claim: Armed personnel roamed the streets and internet shut down in the district
facts.quote: Armed personnel in fatigues roamed the streets, and by the afternoon, the internet had been shut down in the entire district.

facts.claim: Police arrested 26 people in connection to the violence
facts.quote: The police has filed at least eight cases and arrested 26 people in connection to the violence.

facts.claim: Detained activists include youth leaders Otul Jerang, Tajong Talom, their lawyer Sunny Tayeng, and Tongam Rina, the deputy editor of The Arunachal Times
facts.quote: Search warrants were sought from the Chief Judicial Magistrate of Pasighat against youth leaders Otul Jerang, and Tajong Talom, their lawyer Sunny Tayeng, as well as Tongam Rina, the deputy editor of a news publication – The Arunachal Times.

facts.claim: The Arunachal Pradesh Union of Working Journalists and the Arunachal Press Club called the detention of Rina as 'deeply disturbing and a serious threat to press freedom'
facts.quote: The Arunachal Pradesh Union of Working Journalists and the Arunachal Press Club, in a joint statement, called the move against Rina as 'deeply disturbing and a serious threat to press freedom, raising grave concerns over the possible misuse of investigative powers to intimidate journalists reporting on contentious public issues.'

facts.claim: The Siang Indigenous Farmers’ Forum Youth Wing and other groups led protests against the project
facts.quote: Groups such as the Adi Bane Kebang United, SUMP Affected Area Youth Association, Siang Indigenous Farmers’ Forum Youth Wing, and the Adi Galo Welfare Society have banded together to lead protests against the project.

ai.background_note: Residents in Arunachal Pradesh's Siang Valley have protested against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, a hydroelectric and flood-control dam that could affect 27 villages, demanding the release of detained activists and halting pre-feasibility studies.
